Accordingly, in FIG. 11F, in response to speech input 1120, device 1000 displays graphical response 1124 on top of home screen user interface 1122.
In some examples, if the user intent corresponds to at least one of the in-application intents associated with a respective application and the user interface displayed when device 1000 receives the natural language input is not for the respective application, device 1000 displays (e.g., opens, launches, expands, and/or brings to the foreground) the user interface for the respective application. In some examples, displaying the user interface for the respective application includes opening (e.g., launching) the respective applica- tion. 5. Processes for Operating a Digital Assistant
FIG. 12 illustrates process 1200 for operating a digital assistant, according to various examples. Process 1200 is performed, for example, using one or more elec- tronic devices implementing a digital assistant. In some examples, process 1200 is performed using a client-server system (e.g., system 100), and the blocks of process 1200 are divided up in any manner between the server (e.g., DA server 106) and a client device. In other examples, the blocks of process 1200 are divided up between the server and multiple client devices (e.g., a mobile phone and a smart watch). Thus, while portions of process 1200 are described herein as being performed by particular devices of a client- server system, it will be appreciated that process 1200 is not so limited. In other examples, process 1200 is performed using only a client device (e.g., user device 104) or only multiple client devices. In process 1200, some blocks are, optionally, combined, the order of some blocks is, option- ally, changed, and some blocks are, optionally, omitted. In some examples, additional steps may be performed in com- bination with the process 1200.
Process 1200 includes receiving (1202) a first natural language input (e.g., speech input and/or text input) (e.g., 1002, 1010, 1012, and/or 1020) that corresponds to a request to perform a first task with a first application (e.g., a software application) (e.g., at least one of applications 9141-914), wherein the first natural language input speci- fies an entity (e.g., a parameter for the task that is different from the first application) for the first task (e.g., one or more of the entities discussed with respect to FIGS. 10A-10F).
Process 1200 includes in response to (1204) receiv- ing the first natural language input and after the entity is determined (e.g., disambiguated and/or resolved) (e.g., after a specific value is determined for the entity) (e.g., deter- mined by entity resolution module 902): in accordance with a determination (e.g., by type conversion module 904) that (1206) a set of criteria is satisfied, wherein the set of criteria includes a first criterion that is satisfied when a data type (e.g., a file type) for the determined entity does not match (e.g., is incompatible with) a data type (e.g., a file type) accepted by the first application: causing (1208) (e.g., by type conversion module 904) the data type for the deter- mined entity to be modified (e.g., converted and/or trans- formed) to match (e.g., to be compatible with and/or to be the same as) the data type accepted by the first application to obtain a compatible data type for the determined entity (e.g., 910); and initiating (1210) the first task based on the compatible data type for the determined entity (e.g., at least one of the tasks described with respect to FIGS. 10A-10F).
In some examples, process 1200 includes: in response to receiving the first natural language input and after the entity is determined: in accordance with a determination that the set of criteria is not satisfied: forgoing (e.g., by type conversion module 904) causing the data type for the determined entity to be modified to match the data type accepted by the first application; and initiating the first task based on the data type for the determined entity (e.g., the unmodified data type for the determined entity) (e.g., as described with respect to FIGS. 10E-10F). In some examples, the set of criteria is not satisfied when the data type for the determined entity matches a data type accepted by the first application. In some examples, the set of criteria is not satisfied when the application that provides the determined entity (e.g., the application that the determined entity comes from, the application that stores the determined entity, and/or the application that the entity is stored in association with) (e.g., at least one of applications 9141- 914) is the same as the first application.
In some examples, the determined entity is pro- vided by a second application (e.g., the application that the determined entity comes from, the application that stores the determined entity, and/or the application that the entity is stored in association with) (e.g., at least one of applications 9141-914) different from the first application.
In some examples, process 1200 includes: display- ing a user interface for the first application (e.g., 1004, 1008, and/or 1022), wherein the first natural language input is received while the user interface is displayed, and wherein initiating the first task based on the compatible data type for the determined entity includes modifying the user interface (e.g., adding content to the user interface, removing content from the user interface, navigating within the user interface, navigating from the user interface to another user interface for the first application, and/or otherwise modifying the user interface to indicate performance of the task) (e.g., as described with respect to FIGS. 10A-10F).
In some examples, the entity corresponds to contact information (e.g., a phone number, an email address, a username, a user identifier, and/or physical address), to a location, and/or to a media item (e.g., an image, an audio file, and/or a video file).
In some examples, a third application (e.g., soft- ware application) (e.g., at least one of applications 9141- 914) provides, to a first entity database (e.g., 912), a first candidate entity and information about a data type (e.g., a file type) that the first candidate entity can be expressed as (e.g., transformed into, converted into, and/or exported as); and a fourth application (e.g., software application) (e.g., at least one of applications 9141-914) provides, to the first entity database, a second candidate entity and information about a data type that the second candidate entity can be expressed as, wherein the fourth application is different from the third application.
In some examples, the entity is determined (e.g., by entity resolution module 902) by searching the first entity database.
In some examples, the determined entity is the first candidate entity; the compatible data type for the determined entity is the data type that the first candidate entity can be expressed as; and the set of criteria includes a second criterion that is satisfied when the data type that the first candidate entity can be expressed as matches the data type accepted by the first application.
In some examples, the first candidate entity and the information about the data type that the first candidate entity can be expressed as are provided by the third application before receiving the natural language input; and the second candidate entity and the information about the data type that the second candidate entity can be expressed as are provided by the third application before receiving the natural language input.
In some examples, process 1200 includes: initiating (e.g., by entity resolution module 902) a query to a fifth application (e.g., at least one of applications 9141-914), wherein the query requests for one or more entities from the fifth application and information about one or more data types that the one or more entities from the fifth application can be expressed as; and receiving (e.g., by entity resolution module 902 and/or by entity database 912) a response to the query to the fifth application, wherein the response to the query to the fifth application includes the one or more entities from the fifth application and the information about the one or more data types that the one or more entities from the fifth application can be expressed as, wherein the set of criteria includes a third criterion that is satisfied when the response to the query to the fifth application is received (e.g., as described with respect to FIGS. 10C1 and 10D and/or with respect to FIGS. 10C2 and 10D).
In some examples, process 1200 includes: in response to receiving the first natural language input (e.g., 1010): in accordance with a determination that a second entity database (e.g., 912) does not include the entity (e.g., if searching the second entity database for the entity does not yield any matches or, does not yield any matches that have sufficient confidence), initiating (e.g., by entity resolution module 902) a query to a sixth application (e.g., at least one of applications 9141-914) for the entity; and receiving (e.g., by entity resolution module 902 and/or by entity database 912) a response to the query to the sixth application, wherein the response to the query to the sixth application includes the entity (e.g., the determined entity) and information about a data type the entity can be expressed as, wherein the set of criteria includes a fourth criterion that is satisfied when the response to the query to the sixth application is received (e.g., as described with respect to FIGS. 10C1 and 10D). In some examples, the sixth application is queried to determine the entity. In some examples, the set of criteria additionally or alternatively includes another criterion that is satisfied when the data type the entity can be expressed as (as indicated by the response to the query) matches the data type accepted by the first application.
In some examples, process 1200 includes: in response to receiving the first natural language input (e.g., 1012): in accordance with a determination that the natural language input specifies a sixth application (e.g., at least one of applications 9141-914) for the first task, initiating (e.g., by entity resolution module 902) a query to the sixth application for the entity; and receiving (e.g., by entity resolution module 902 and/or by entity database 912) a response to the query to the sixth application, wherein the response to the query to the sixth application includes the entity (e.g., the determined entity) and information about a data type the entity can be expressed as, wherein the set of criteria includes a fourth criterion that is satisfied when the response to the query to the sixth application is received (e.g., as described with respect to FIGS. 10C2 and 10D). In some examples, the sixth application is queried to determine the entity. In some examples, the set of criteria additionally or alternatively include another criterion that is satisfied when the data type the entity can be expressed as (as indicated by the response to the query) matches the data type accepted by the first application.
In some examples, the first application defines one or more data types accepted by the first application.
In some examples, the data type accepted by the first application is determined (e.g., by type conversion module 904) based on the first natural language input. In some examples, the data type accepted by the first appli- cation is determined by determining, based on the first natural language input, a type (e.g., phone number, email, location, image, and/or video) for the entity and selecting, from a plurality of data types accepted by the application (e.g., string, GPS coordinates, .jpeg, .png, .mov, .mp4, and the like) the accepted data types that match the entity type.
In some examples, process 1200 includes: receiv- ing a second natural language input (e.g., 1032) that corre- sponds to a request to perform a second task with a seventh application (e.g., at least one of applications 9141-914), wherein the second natural language input specifies a second entity for the second task (e.g., as described with respect to FIG. 10G).
In some examples, process 1200 includes: in response to receiving the second natural language input, displaying a selectable option for the second entity (e.g., 1034, 1036, and/or 1036(1)). In some examples, process 1200 includes displaying a list of multiple different options for the second entity (e.g., 1036), wherein the option is included in the list of multiple different options. In some examples, the multiple different options correspond to respective different interpretations (e.g., possible disam- biguation options) for the second entity. In some examples, process 1200 includes displaying the selectable option and/ or the list of multiple different options in accordance with a determination that the entity is ambiguous and/or that the device cannot disambiguate the entity.
In some examples, process 1200 includes receiving a user input (e.g., touch input, speech input, gesture input, peripheral device input, and/or gaze input) (e.g., 1038) corresponding to a selection of the selectable option for the second entity. In some examples, the device determines the second entity based on the user input.

FIG. 13 illustrates process 1300 for operating a digital assistant, according to various examples. Process 1300 is performed, for example, using one or more elec- tronic devices implementing a digital assistant. In some examples, process 1300 is performed using a client-server system (e.g., system 100), and the blocks of process 1300 are divided up in any manner between the server (e.g., DA server 106) and a client device. In other examples, the blocks of process 1300 are divided up between the server and multiple client devices (e.g., a mobile phone and a smart watch). Thus, while portions of process 1300 are described herein as being performed by particular devices of a client- server system, it will be appreciated that process 1300 is not so limited. In other examples, process 1300 is performed using only a client device (e.g., user device 104) or only multiple client devices. In process 1300, some blocks are, optionally, combined, the order of some blocks is, option- ally, changed, and some blocks are, optionally, omitted. In some examples, additional steps may be performed in com- bination with the process 1300.
Process 1300 includes: while displaying a user interface for an application (e.g., 1104, 1132, 1004, 1008, and/or 1022) (e.g., a software application), receiving (1302) a natural language input (e.g., 1102, 1108, 1130, 1002, 1010, 1012, and/or 1020) (e.g., speech input and/or text input).
Process 1300 includes: in response to (1304) receiving the natural language input: in accordance with a determination that (1306) a user intent corresponds to (e.g., matches and/or corresponds to a same type of task as) a predetermined intent associated with the application (e.g., that the user intent corresponds to at least one intent of a predetermined set of intents associated with the application), wherein the user intent is determined based on the natural language input (and optionally in accordance with a deter- mination that a digital assistant session is initiated): initiat- ing (1308) a first task based on the user intent, wherein initiating the first task includes initiating a search (e.g., for data within the application and/or for data from another application), and wherein initiating the first task includes modifying the user interface for the application, without displaying, outside of the user interface for the application (e.g., outside of any user interface for the application), a (e.g., any) graphical response that is based on the user intent (e.g., without displaying any portion of the graphical response outside (e.g., over, under, or adjacent to) the user interface for the application, e.g., such that the graphical response is entirely contained within the user interface for the application) (e.g., as illustrated by FIGS. 11A-11B, 11G-111, 10A-10B, 10C1-10D, 10C2-10D, and 10E-10F). In some examples, modifying the user interface for the appli- cation includes displaying a graphical response that is based on the user intent, where the graphical response is contained within (e.g., entirely contained within) and/or inside (e.g., entirely inside) the user interface for the application (e.g., any user interface for the application). In some examples, initiating the search includes initiating a search for data local to the user device and/or data stored in association with the user and/or the user's account, e.g., data that requires the user to be authenticated for access to the data. In some examples, initiating the search includes searching external sources (e.g., the internet).
In some examples, the predetermined intent asso- ciated with the application corresponds to a predetermined type of action a digital assistant can cause the application to per- form. In some examples, an application is associated with a predetermined set of intents, where each intent of the predetermined set of intents corresponds to a different action a digital assistant can cause the application to perform.
In some examples, process 1300 includes: in response to receiving the natural language input: in accor- dance with a determination that the user intent does not correspond to a predetermined intent associated with the first application (e.g., that the user intent does not correspond to any intent of the predetermined set of intents associated with the application): initiating a second task based on the user intent, wherein initiating the second task includes dis- playing, outside of the user interface for the appli- cation, a second graphical response that is based on the user intent (e.g., displaying the second graphical response at least partially over, under, and/or adjacent to the user interface for the application, such that at least a portion of the second graphical response is outside of the user interface for the application) (e.g., as illustrated by FIGS. 11C-11D).
In some examples, process 1300 includes: while displaying a current user interface (e.g., 1122), receiving a second natural language input (e.g., 1120) that corresponds to (e.g., requests for) the same first task; and in response to receiving the second natural language input: in accordance with a determination that the current user interface is not the user interface for the application (e.g., is not user interface 1104) (e.g., is not any user interface for the application): initiating the first task, wherein initiating the first task includes displaying, outside of the current user interface, a third graphical response (e.g., 1124) (e.g., as illustrated by FIGS. 11E-11F). In some examples, process 1300 includes: in response to receiving the second natural language input and in accordance with a determination that the current user interface is a/the user interface for the application, initiating the first task, wherein initiating the first task includes modifying the user interface for the application, without display- ing, outside of the user interface for the application, any graphical response that is based on the user intent.
In some examples, modifying the user interface for the application includes modifying the user interface for the application to indicate results of the search (e.g., to indicate results of a search for messages, to indicate results of a search for media content, to indicate results of a search for notes, to indicate results of a search for photos, or the like) (e.g., as illustrated by FIGS. 11A-11B, 11G-111, 10A-10B, 10C1-10D, 10C2-10D, and 10E-10F).
In some examples, the user interface for the appli- cation includes a map user interface (e.g., 1104) and wherein modifying the user interface for the application to indicate the results of the search includes indicating (e.g., via 1106 (1)-1106(3)) one or more locations on the map user interface (e.g., as pins on the map).
In some examples, initiating the first task includes navigating (e.g., scrolling, changing to a next section, changing to a previous section, and/or replacing the user interface for the application with another user interface for the application) with respect to the user interface for the application (e.g., as illustrated by FIGS. 11G-111).
In some examples, initiating the first task includes performing a text editing operation (e.g., adding content, deleting content, changing a property (e.g., color, font size, and the like) of the content, and/or selecting content) and wherein modifying the user interface for the application includes indicating a result of the text editing operation (e.g., as illustrated by FIGS. 10C1-10D and 10C2-10D).
In some examples, modifying the user interface for the application includes: in accordance with a determination that the first task satisfies a set of criteria: displaying a first type of animation (e.g., 1134) (e.g., an animation that includes pulsing and/or blurring the current user interface); and in accordance with a determination that the first task does not satisfy the set of criteria: modifying the user interface for the application without displaying the first type of animation. In some examples, the first type of animation transitions the user interface for the application to a different user interface for the application.
In some examples, the set of criteria includes a first criterion that is satisfied when initiating the first task includes replacing the user interface for the application (e.g., 1132) with a different second user interface for the applica- tion (e.g., 1136) (e.g., switching between sections, pages, menus, and/or tabs of the application).
In some examples, the set of criteria include a second criterion that is satisfied when a user of the electronic device cannot perform the first task via the user interface for the application (e.g., 1132) (e.g., cannot manually perform the task, e.g., cannot perform the task without requesting the digital assistant to perform the task). In some examples, the user instead navigates to a different user interface for the application (e.g., 1136) to be able to perform the task, e.g., because the user interface for the application does not include the correct controls to perform the task.
In some examples, the user interface for the appli- cation (e.g., 1132) does not include one or more controls (e.g., one or more graphical elements selectable to cause the application to perform respective operations) to perform the first task; a different user interface for the application (e.g., 1136) includes the one or more controls to perform the first task; and the user cannot perform the first task via the user interface for the application because the user interface for the application does not include the one or more controls to perform the first task. In some examples, the set of criteria includes a third criterion that is satisfied when the user interface for the application does not include one or more controls to perform the first task and when a different user interface for the application includes the one or more controls to perform the first task.
In some examples, process 1300 includes: while displaying a respective user interface (e.g., 1174 or 1176), receiving a user input (e.g., 1155 or 1178) corresponding to a request to insert content (e.g., 1160 or 1183) (e.g., text, a photo, a video, and/or another graphical element) (e.g., to add content and/or to replace previously entered content with new content) and in response to receiving the user input: in accordance with a determination that the user input satisfies a set of input criteria: inserting the content into the respective user interface, including displaying an animation (e.g., 1158 or 1182) that moves through the content in a first direction (e.g., left to right, right to left, up to down, or down to up), wherein the content includes a first portion (e.g., 1162, 1164, 1166, 1168, 1184, 1185, or 1186), a second portion (e.g., 1164, 1166, 1168, 1170, 1185, 1186, or 1187) that follows, relative to the first direction, the first portion, and a third portion (e.g., 1166, 1168, 1170, 1172, 1186, 1187, or 1188), that follows, relative to the first direction, the second portion.
Displaying the animation includes: at a first time (e.g., times T1, T2, T3, T4, T5, T6, or T7 in FIGS. 11L1- 11L8 or times T1, T2, T3, T4, T5, T6, or T7 in FIGS. 1101-1102): displaying the first portion such that a first visual parameter (e.g., color, brightness, opacity, or size) of the first portion has a first value (e.g., first color, first brightness, first opacity, or first size); at a second time after the first time: displaying the first portion such that the first visual parameter of the first portion has a sec- ond value different from the first value; and displaying the second portion such that a sec- ond visual parameter of the second portion has the first value; and at a third time after the second time: displaying the first portion such that the first visual parameter of the first portion has a third value different from the first value and the second value; displaying the second portion such that the second visual parameter of the second portion has the second value; and displaying the third portion such that a third visual parameter of the third portion has the first value, wherein the first visual parameter, the second visual parameter, and the third visual parameter are the same type of visual param- eter.
In some examples, process 1300 includes in response to receiving the user input, in accordance with a determination that the user input does not satisfy the set of input criteria, forgoing displaying the animation. In some examples, the animation completes when the respective visual parameters of all portions of the content each have the same value, e.g., an end value. In some examples, the insertion of the content completes when the animation completes. In some examples, the first visual parameter of the first portion has the first value when the animation begins and the first visual parameter of the first portion gradually changes to have an end value as the animation progresses. When a visual parameter of a respective portion has the end value, the visual parameter of the respective portion no longer changes as the animation progresses. In some examples, the animation completes when the respective visual parameters of each portion of the content each have the end value, as described and illustrated herein.
In accordance with a determination that the content has a first size (e.g., area, volume, length, or word count), the animation has a first speed (e.g., that defines how quickly the animation completes); and in accordance with a determination that the content has a second size that is larger than the first size, the anima- tion has a second speed that is greater than the first speed. In some examples, the speed of the animation depends on the size of the content being inserted, such that all insertions of content via the animation appear to complete within the same time, regardless of the size of the content being inserted.
Conditionally displaying the animation (e.g., 1158 or 1182) as described herein provides the user with improved feedback that the device is inserting text via a particular type of process (e.g., a digital assistant process and/or a generative artificial intelligence process). Providing improved user feedback makes the user-device interface more efficient (e.g., by informing the user that the device is operating as desired, by preventing user inputs otherwise received if the user believes the device is not operating as desired, and by distinguishing between different types of text insertion methods), which additionally reduces power usage and improves battery life of the device by enabling the user to use the device more quickly and efficiently.
